correctness.rationale: Use the Exner-Kostenko-Malamud-Neidhardt Theorem 3.5 correspondence from minimal Kirchhoff quantum Laplacian to weighted discrete h0 with m(v)=sum incident edge lengths and b=1/edge length. At z=+i and -i terminal tooth equation gives f_leaf=f_k/(1-z*a^2), |denominator|>=1. The spine flux p_k=(f_k-f_(k+1))/ell_k obeys p1=z*q1*f1 and p_k-p_(k-1)=z*q_k*f_k, with |q_k|<=m(c_k)+a_(k,+)+a_(k,-) summable. All solutions determined by single f1 (dim <=1); summable transfer coefficients imply bounded solution for f1=1; total vertex weight =2 sum lengths finite implies it belongs to ell2(m) (dim >=1). Thus n_+(H0)=n_-(H0)=1 for arbitrary asymmetric tooth lengths. The actual package finite exact-rational checker was read; that check only supports the recurrence, not the infinite tail.

originality.rationale: Exner et al., arXiv:1705.01831, Theorem 3.5 and Example 4.18, discuss precisely finite-length shrinking combs and explicitly leave index=1 as an expectation while establishing non-self-adjointness. Kostenko-Mugnolo-Nicolussi (2022), Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.3, Remark 4.12, give general one-finite-volume-end lower bound and some symmetry-dependent equality conclusions, not the upper bound for arbitrarily unequal paired teeth. The direct scalar spine recurrence removes that extra symmetry condition. A weakly indexed decorated Jacobi formulation may already derive the same equality.
